title: Photosynthesis, Respiration and Cycles in Nature
seo_title: Grade 8 Science: Photosynthesis, Respiration and Cycles in Nature Worksheets (MATATAG)
standard_text: Photosynthesis makes glucose and oxygen from carbon dioxide and water using light; respiration releases energy from glucose; the two processes link the carbon and oxygen cycles; water and nitrogen also cycle in nature. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 8, Quarter 1: Life Science)
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 1: Life Science): photosynthesis, factors affecting it, respiration, comparing the processes and the carbon and water cycles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Photosynthesis stores energy; respiration releases it.
key_sub: Carbon cycles between the air and living things.
body_html:
How to think about it

Photosynthesis happens in chloroplasts: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen, using light energy. Light intensity, carbon dioxide and temperature affect its rate.

Respiration happens in mitochondria: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water + energy. Together, photosynthesis and respiration move carbon and oxygen between living things and the air; decomposers and burning also return carbon dioxide.

Example

Which gas do plants take in for photosynthesis?

They give out oxygen.

Answer: carbon dioxide

Example

Where does respiration happen?

The powerhouse of the cell

Answer: in the mitochondria

Common mistakes

  • Thinking plants do not respire.
  • Thinking plants get food from the soil.
  • Thinking respiration is the same as breathing.

faq.q: Why are forests called carbon sinks?
faq.a: Trees take in carbon dioxide and store carbon in wood.

faq.q: Why does burning fossil fuels affect the carbon cycle?
faq.a: It releases carbon that was stored underground for millions of years.

items.q: Kristine observes: “A civet breathes out carbon dioxide.” What does this show about matter in the ecosystem?
c: Nitrogen cycles from the soil into plants.
Matter and energy in the grass move into the rabbit.
Carbon from the air becomes part of the plant.
Carbon goes back into the air, where plants can take it in.
items.e: Matter cycles among living and nonliving parts of the ecosystem.

items.q: Emmanuel observes: “Plants take in carbon dioxide during photosynthesis.” What does this show about matter in the ecosystem?
c: Decomposers return carbon and nutrients to the air and soil.
Nitrogen cycles from the soil into plants.
Carbon from the air becomes part of the plant.
Nutrients return to the soil for plants to use again.
items.e: Matter cycles among living and nonliving parts of the ecosystem.

items.q: Where do the atoms in your body come from?

items.q: Is energy recycled in an ecosystem?
